requirement:
When a provider reports a transient failure, the harness MUST wait and retry
the same completion request. Transient failures are throttling, reported
through HTTP 429 or a Bedrock `ThrottlingException`; temporary unavailability,
reported through HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 or a Bedrock
`ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, or
`ModelNotReadyException`; and a request with no response after ten minutes,
which the harness MUST abandon. The retry MUST retain its prompt, history,
tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
retries.

The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
transient failure, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request, and interruption MUST cancel both the
wait and further retries.

Each attempt MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider` {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`
rationale:
The implementation and subject-marked tests satisfy `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff`.

### Obligations and coverage

- **Wait and retry the same request for HTTP 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 and each named Bedrock exception.** `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[ProviderBackoff]/fn[next_delay]` classifies these structured signals; `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` sleeps and retries. Coverage: `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[retries_throttling_unavailability_and_timeouts_but_not_permanent_errors]`, `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[transient_bedrock_codes_retry_whatever_their_http_status]`, and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[throttled_requests_retry_unchanged_and_record_every_attempt]`. `rig_failures_keep_their_provider_report_for_backoff` in the providers test module also verifies preservation of the structured failure signals.
- **Abandon a request unanswered for ten minutes and retry it.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#const[REQUEST_TIMEOUT]` supplies 600 seconds to the timeout in `converse`. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unanswered_requests_are_abandoned_and_retried]` exercises this path and checks the two recorded outcomes.
- **Retain prompt, history, tools, and pending inputs; do not restart the assessment or repeat completed tool calls.** `converse` clones the existing request and continues its retry loop before changing conversation state or dispatching tools. The unchanged-request test above checks complete serialized request equality. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[success_resets_backoff_and_retries_keep_history_without_repeating_tools]` additionally checks equality after a tool turn, retained tool results, a single read-tool execution, and resulting evidence inputs.
- **Keep permanent input/context-length, authentication, and invalid-request failures as errors; do not retry merely because a message mentions tokens.** `next_delay` uses status/code metadata rather than message text and returns no delay for permanent failures. The classification test covers validation and access-denial errors and an unstructured token message. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[permanent_provider_failure_returns_without_waiting_or_retrying]` verifies immediate error propagation, one attempt, and a non-retried failure record.
- **Start the window at one second, double it after consecutive transient failures, cap it at sixty seconds, and randomly choose each delay between half and all of the window.** `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[ProviderBackoff/Default]/fn[default]` initializes the window; `next_delay` doubles/caps it and samples with `fastrand`. `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[jittered_backoff_grows_to_a_ceiling]` checks the successive bounds through 100 failures.
- **Honor Retry-After seconds and HTTP dates as minimum delays, including values beyond the window.** `src/authoring/providers.rs#fn[retry_after]` parses both forms, and `next_delay` takes the maximum of that minimum and jitter. `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[retry_after_accepts_seconds_and_dates_without_shortening_provider_delay]` checks both forms and a ninety-second minimum. The retry deadline in `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[ProviderBackoff]/fn[retry]` is separately specified by `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff.limit`, which that code and `converse` also mark: it explicitly requires stopping when Retry-After would pass the one-minute retry deadline. Thus this stopping behavior is specified, not an extra behavior.
- **Reset backoff after success.** `converse` replaces backoff with its default after a successful completion. `success_resets_backoff_and_retries_keep_history_without_repeating_tools` verifies that both retry sequences use the initial window.
- **Interruption cancels waiting and further retries.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[author_evidence_with_options]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[prepare_assessment]` select cancellation against assessment execution, dropping the outstanding wait/request future. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cancelling_during_backoff_prevents_another_request]` drops execution during backoff, advances time, and verifies no additional attempt. Testing actual Ctrl-C delivery would require process-wide signal state; the direct cancellation test exercises the dropped-future behavior without it.
- **Record every attempt under the usage requirement.** `converse` brackets every attempt, including timeout and retry attempts, with `UsageLog::begin_request` and `UsageLog::end_request`, then marks retries with `UsageLog::retried` (`src/authoring/usage.rs`). The unchanged-request and unanswered-request tests assert attempt counts and outcomes; the former also checks structured failures and unavailable usage on failures. This verifies application of `requirements.authoring.usage_requests` without reassessing that requirement independently.
- **Disable hidden SDK retries.** `src/authoring/providers.rs#fn[bedrock_sdk_config]` reaches `bedrock_sdk_loader`, which explicitly configures disabled AWS retries. `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bedrock_sdk_retries_are_disabled]` checks one maximum attempt. The OpenAI/Ollama connection paths use Rig's direct transport without adding a retry layer.
- **Do not report transient recovery as a finished judgment or terminal assessment error.** `converse` continues after recording and waiting on a recoverable failure; it reaches submission handling only after success. The throttled-request test verifies eventual success and exactly one submission after five failed attempts; the timeout test verifies successful recovery as well.
- **Record pending evidence inputs only after success.** `converse` calls `sources.record_inputs` and clears pending inputs only after the successful-response branch. The unchanged-request test checks delivery on the successful attempt, the tool-history test checks retained additional-read evidence, and the cancellation test checks that no evidence inputs were recorded when recovery was interrupted.

The implementation helpers are reachable from the subject's marked roots, and the tests cited above carry subject test references. No acknowledged or unacknowledged gap was found.

:::{req} usage_requests
Usage MUST record each provider request's outcome and available input/output
token counts, including retries, with cached or reasoning-token counts when
provided, and for a failed request the failure under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests.failures`. Missing measurements MUST be recorded as unavailable, not zero.
Run totals MUST include request and tool-call counts by tool, elapsed time, and
available token usage, identifying incomplete totals without double counting
provider counters that overlap.
:::{req} provider
The authoring harness MUST use Rig and support Bedrock, Ollama, and OpenAI. Users MUST be
able to select a backend and model through configuration without changing the
assessment tools, prompt, or evidence format.
:::{req} delivered_inputs
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs and additional reads, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
:::{req} provider_backoff.limit
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
